children: State-run Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) said on Monday that its board of directors has approved the 425 km-long Kochi-Kanyakumari-Thoothukudi natural gas pipeline (KPTL), which will enhance gas supply in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

IOCL’s Board cleared the investment approval for laying, building and operating KTPL at an estimated project cost of ₹2,448.70 crore with a system capacity, including common carrier capacity, of 6.84 million standard cubic metres per day (MSCMD).

The common carrier capacity of the pipeline will be at least 1.71 MSCMD. Common carrier capacity refers to the unutilised capacity in a pipeline that is made available to third-parties for transporting gas.

The pipeline will originate from Petronet LNG’s (PLL) terminal in Kochi and will connect to IOCL’s Ennore-Thiruvallur-Bengaluru-Puducherry-Nagapattinam-Madurai-Thoothukudi Natural Gas Pipeline (ETBPNMTPL) at Thoothukudi.
The pipeline will start from the Kochi LNG terminal and connect to Kottayam–Kottarakkara-Kattakkada-Nagercoil-Thoothukudi and end at IOCL’s ETBPNMTPL.

The pipeline, once operational will boost the capacity utilisation of PLL’s Kochi liquified natural gas (LNG) terminal, which has been faced with low capacity utilisation due to lack of evacuating infrastructure (pipeline) to major demand centres in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

In FY26, the Kochi terminal with a capacity of 5 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) recorded a capacity utilisation of mere 26.3 per cent with a total send out of 1.31 mtpa, its highest since commencement of operations in 2013. In Q1 FY27, its capacity utilisation stood at 23.27 per cent.

The pipeline, once operational will ensure further expansion of city gas distribution (CGD) networks as well as ensure gas supply to industries, particularly in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, an industry source said.

In a bid to boost utilisation of the Kochi LNG terminal, Petronet LNG is exploring LNG bunkering services as a new growth avenue, aligned with the evolving maritime fuel transition and global adoption of LNG as a cleaner marine fuel. Following the expected growth in container and trans-shipment traffic, market interactions suggest a favourable demand outlook for LNG bunkering services from international shipping operators and accordingly, bunkering facilities are being upgraded at Kochi terminal, it said in its FY26 annual report.

Besides, to promote LNG as a cleaner energy source for industrial applications and long-haul transportation, PLL aims to augment its LNG truck-loading capacity at Kochi. Actions have been initiated to add two truck-loading facility (TLF) bays at Kochi, taking its total from four to six numbers bays.

title: Indian Oil board approves Kochi-Kanyakumari-Thoothukudi gas pipeline
